items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: So the thing is this Mussorgsky piece has been arranged probably

ctx.x: where you are. Like is this measure 49 or is it 50 of my rests. Is this something that ever happened to you?

Oh yeah. Yeah that’s happened. But that’s part of the deal. That happens in Rachmaninoff’s Symphonic Dances you know the only thing the alto saxophone does is play a solo. It’s in a bunch of sharps and you play it at about, I don’t know, about ten minutes into the piece. So you’re there, your reed is dried out, could have lost suction, you know you never know what’s going to happen there. But I’ll tell you one of the roughest things the “Pictures at an Exhibition” was written by Mussorgsky, okay? And it was the…
That whole mindset of playing exactly what someone else has written and being in the jazz world is, I don’t have an exact comment except it’s such as different way of being in your head.
